The '''2000 FA Charity Shield''' (also known as The One 2 One FA Charity Shield for sponsorship reasons) was the 78th [[FA Community Shield|FA Charity Shield]], an annual [[association football|football]] match organised by [[the Football Association]], and contested by the winners of the previous season's [[Premier League]] and [[FA Cup]] competitions. It was the final club match played at the original [[Wembley Stadium (1923)|Wembley Stadium]] in London and took place on 13 August 2000 between [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]], the winners of the [[1999–2000 FA Cup]], and [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]], who had won the [[1999–2000 FA Premier League]]. Watched by a crowd of 65,148, Chelsea won the match 2–0.

This was Chelsea's 4th appearance in the Shield and Manchester United's 20th. It was the second time they had met in the competition. Chelsea were without [[Albert Ferrer]], who had sustained a chest injury in pre-season, while [[Graeme Le Saux]] made his first appearance in 10 months after recovering from an ankle injury. Three of Chelsea's new signings made their debuts for the team, with [[Jimmy Floyd Hasselbaink]], [[Eiður Guðjohnsen]] and [[Mario Stanić]] named in the squad, while goalkeeper [[Fabien Barthez]] was Manchester United's only debutant.

Chelsea took the lead in the 22nd minute when Hasselbaink's shot deflected off [[Jaap Stam]] and over Barthez after the Dutch striker was put through on goal by a [[Gus Poyet]] [[Header (association football)|header]]. Manchester United captain [[Roy Keane]] was shown a [[Penalty card#Red card|red card]] midway through the second half for a [[Tackle (football move)#Association football|tackle]] on Poyet. Minutes later, Chelsea scored a second goal through [[Mario Melchiot]], who shot left-footed low past the legs of Stam and Barthez. No further goals were scored and Chelsea took the Charity Shield for the second time, 45 years after their first in [[1955 FA Charity Shield|1955]]. It was the third year in succession that Manchester United had been defeated in the competition, the first club to suffer the feat.

==Background==
[[File:Wembleyold.jpg|thumb|[[Wembley Stadium (1923)|Wembley Stadium]] played host to the Charity Shield for the 27th and final time.]]
Founded in 1908 as a successor to the [[Sheriff of London Charity Shield]],<ref>{{cite news |title=Abandonment of the Sheriff Shield |page=11 |newspaper=[[The Observer]] |location=London |date=19 April 1908 }}</ref> the [[FA Community Shield|FA Charity Shield]] began as a contest between the respective champions of the [[English Football League|Football League]] and the [[Southern Football League|Southern League]], although in 1913 it was played between an Amateurs XI and a Professionals XI.<ref>{{cite news |title=The F.A. Charity Shield |page=10 |newspaper=[[The Times]] |date=7 October 1913 }}</ref> In 1921, it was played by the [[Football League First Division|First Division]] champions and [[FA Cup]] winners for the first time.<ref>{{cite news |first=Peter |last=Ferguson |title=The Shield: From the beginning |url=http://www.mcfc.co.uk/news/team-news/archive/2011/august/community-shield-2011/the-shield-from-the-beginning |publisher=Manchester City FC |date=4 August 2011 |access-date=21 April 2014 |archive-date=4 March 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304192421/http://www.mcfc.co.uk/news/team-news/archive/2011/august/community-shield-2011/the-shield-from-the-beginning |url-status=dead }}</ref>{{refn|The [[Premier League]] replaced the [[Football League First Division]] at the top of the [[English football league system|English football pyramid]] after its inception in 1992.<ref>{{cite news |title=Continental or the full English? |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2001/dec/02/sport.sportfeatures |first=Alex |last=Fynn |newspaper=The Observer |location=London |date=2 December 2001 |access-date=3 July 2014 }}</ref>|group=lower-alpha}} The match in 2000 was the 27th and last Charity Shield to be played at the [[Wembley Stadium (1923)|original Wembley Stadium]] before it was demolished for renovation.<ref>{{cite news|title=The FA Community Shield history |url=http://www.thefa.com/fa-community-shield/more/history |publisher=[[The Football Association]]|access-date=3 July 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130609184712/http://www.thefa.com/fa-community-shield/more/history |archive-date=9 June 2013 |url-status=live |df=dmy }}</ref> The host broadcaster was [[Sky Sports]], who provided main commentary from [[Martin Tyler]] and [[Andy Gray (footballer, born 1955)|Andy Gray]], as well as an alternative feed dubbed "FanZone" via the interactive [[Sky UK|Sky Digital]] platform, with a fan from each team providing commentary.<ref>{{cite web|title=FanZone – The Alternative Commentary|url=http://www.sky.com/sports/football/story24.htm|website=[[Sky Sports]]|date=2000|access-date=10 March 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20000815200128/http://www.sky.com/sports/football/story24.htm|archive-date=15 August 2000|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|last=Barlow|first=Matt|title=Football: Sky eager to avoid pay row|url=https://link.gale.com/apps/doc/A63979008/GPS?u=wikipedia&sid=GPS&xid=3e76229a|work=[[The Independent]]|date=10 August 2000|access-date=10 March 2020|page=22|via=Gale General OneFile|url-access=subscription}}</ref>

Chelsea qualified by way of winning the [[1999–2000 FA Cup]], their second FA Cup title in the previous four years.<ref name=DTAussieReport>{{cite news|title=Spotlight on United yet again|url=https://link.gale.com/apps/doc/A103648522/GPS?u=wikipedia&sid=GPS&xid=f8744c95|work=[[The Daily Telegraph (Sydney)|The Daily Telegraph]]|date=12 August 2000|access-date=10 March 2020|page=156|via=Gale OneFile: News|url-access=subscription}}</ref> They defeated [[Aston Villa F.C.|Aston Villa]] 1–0 [[2000 FA Cup Final|in the final]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/sport/football/fa_cup/756784.stm|title=Chelsea claim FA Cup glory|date=20 May 2000|website=[[BBC Sport]]|access-date=10 March 2020}}</ref> Manchester United had qualified for the Charity Shield by winning the [[1999–2000 FA Premier League]], their sixth league championship in eight years.<ref name="DTAussieReport" /> They had scored a league-high 97 goals and won the title by a then-record margin of 18 points over second-placed [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.premierleague.com/news/693624|title=1999/00 Season Review|date=25 May 2018|publisher=[[Premier League]]|access-date=10 March 2020}}</ref> Chelsea were appearing in the Charity Shield for a fourth time; they had won in their first appearance in [[1955 FA Charity Shield|1955]], and lost in [[1970 FA Charity Shield|1970]] and [[1997 FA Charity Shield|1997]]. This was Manchester United's 20th appearance in the competition; they had won ten ([[1908 FA Charity Shield|1908]], [[1911 FA Charity Shield|1911]], [[1952 FA Charity Shield|1952]], [[1956 FA Charity Shield|1956]], [[1957 FA Charity Shield|1957]], [[1983 FA Charity Shield|1983]], [[1993 FA Charity Shield|1993]], [[1994 FA Charity Shield|1994]], [[1996 FA Charity Shield|1996]], 1997), shared four ([[1965 FA Charity Shield|1965]], [[1967 FA Charity Shield|1967]], [[1977 FA Charity Shield|1977]], [[1990 FA Charity Shield|1990]]) and lost five ([[1948 FA Charity Shield|1948]], [[1963 FA Charity Shield|1963]], [[1985 FA Charity Shield|1985]], [[1998 FA Charity Shield|1998]] and [[1999 FA Charity Shield|1999]]). By their fifth consecutive appearance, United surpassed the record of four they shared with [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]] and [[Everton F.C.|Everton]], who respectively achieved that feat between [[1933 FA Charity Shield|1933]] and [[1936 FA Charity Shield|1936]], and [[1984 FA Charity Shield|1984]] and [[1987 FA Charity Shield|1987]]. The 2000 match was the second meeting between these two clubs in the Shield; Manchester United won the previous encounter in 1997 4–2 in a [[Penalty shoot-out (association football)|penalty shoot-out]] after a 1–1 draw in normal time.<ref>{{cite web |first=James |last=Ross |title=List of FA Charity/Community Shield Matches |url=https://www.rsssf.org/tablese/engsupcuphist.html |date=15 August 2013 |website=[[RSSSF]] |access-date=11 January 2014 }}</ref>

==Pre-match==
Manchester United manager [[Alex Ferguson]] said before the match that he was pleased that his side was one of the teams to play in the final Charity Shield match to be contested at the old Wembley Stadium and was hoping the win could give the team a good start stating: "The Charity Shield is not the most important fixture, but nonetheless it is preparation – and in preparation you want to do well. We want to see some progress from the games that we've had so far and the training."<ref name="BBCPreview">{{cite web|title=Sir Alex relishes final call|url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport/hi/english/football/teams/m/man_utd/newsid_878000/878622.stm|website=BBC Sport|date=13 August 2000|access-date=10 March 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20000824032343/http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport/hi/english/football/teams/m/man_utd/newsid_878000/878622.stm|archive-date=24 August 2000|url-status=dead}}</ref> [[Gianluca Vialli]], the Chelsea manager, used his press conference to emphasise that new signings [[Jimmy Floyd Hasselbaink]] and [[Eiður Guðjohnsen]] would score additional goals for the club and spoke of the Charity Shield's significance, saying: "It is a very important match for us as we can win a trophy and put it in our cabinet. That would be the best way to start a new season – beating the champions at Wembley and winning a trophy."<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.sky.com/sports/football/premier/chelsea/story1.htm|title=Goals On Their Way To The Bridge|date=12 August 2000|website=Sky Sports|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20000815200106/http://www.sky.com/sports/football/premier/chelsea/story1.htm|archive-date=15 August 2000|access-date=10 March 2020}}</ref>

[[Phil Neville]], a [[Defender (association football)|defender]] for Manchester United, was told by Ferguson to expect verbal abuse from the spectators during the match because he was blamed for bringing about [[England national football team|England]]'s exit from [[UEFA Euro 2000]] after a 3–2 defeat to [[Romania national football team|Romania]] two months prior. He had already received abuse in a pre-season [[Exhibition game|friendly match]] against [[Shrewsbury Town F.C.|Shrewsbury Town]] of which Ferguson said: "When you play away from home, you're hardly going to get bouquets of flowers thrown at you. That's not going to change, but I think Phil is capable of handling it. I expect his team-mates to help him through it. That's what teams are about. That's what the word 'team' means."<ref name=TimesAbuse>{{Cite news|last=Kay|first=Oliver|url=https://link.gale.com/apps/doc/A64266097/GPS?u=wikipedia&sid=GPS&xid=a049caad|title=Ferguson tells Neville to expect crowd abuse; Football Saturday|date=12 August 2000|work=The Times|access-date=10 March 2020|page=31|via=Gale Academic OneFile|url-access=subscription}}</ref>

Paul Johnson of ''[[Racing Post]]'' opined that Chelsea would be the team more likely to win the Charity Shield even though the two clubs had each won 8 of their last 16 encounters.<ref name="RPPreview">{{cite news|last=Johnson|first=Paul|url=https://link.gale.com/apps/doc/A64144689/GPS?u=wikipedia&sid=GPS&xid=9d9c614e|title=Football: Charity case is made for draw; Share of the spoils rates a sound investment at 12–5|date=13 August 2000|work=Racing Post|access-date=10 March 2020|page=79|via=Gale OneFile: News|url-access=subscription}}</ref> The football correspondent of the Sydney-based ''[[The Daily Telegraph (Sydney)|Daily Telegraph]]'' wrote that other clubs will focus on Manchester United's weaknesses rather than the final score of the match.<ref name="DTAussieReport" /> [[Mike Riley (referee)|Mike Riley]] was selected as the [[Referee (association football)|referee]] for the match;<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://link.gale.com/apps/doc/A291452130/GPS?u=wikipedia&sid=GPS&xid=1231cb77|title=Season warm-up likely to be hot stuff|date=13 August 2000|work=[[The Age|The Sunday Age]]|access-date=10 March 2020|page=22|via=Gale OneFile: News|url-access=subscription}}</ref> [[Uriah Rennie]] was originally slated to take charge of the match before it was discovered that he had been demoted from the list of Premier League referees, and he ultimately served as [[Assistant referee (association football)#Fourth official|fourth official]].<ref>{{Cite news|last=Kempson|first=Russell|url=https://link.gale.com/apps/doc/A64183289/GPS?u=wikipedia&sid=GPS&xid=4bd715d8|title=Uriah weep; Wembley notebook|date=14 August 2000|work=The Times|access-date=11 March 2020|page=3|via=Gale Academic OneFile|url-access=subscription}}</ref> Neither club sold out their allocation of tickets, with Chelsea selling 27,000 out of 30,000 reserved.<ref name="CFCPreview">{{cite web|title=Charity Shield Build Up|url=http://www.chelseafc.co.uk/chelsea/news/news_11800_1632.shtml|publisher=Chelsea F.C|date=11 August 2000|access-date=10 March 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20001025195630/http://www.chelseafc.co.uk/chelsea/news/news_11800_1632.shtml|archive-date=25 October 2000|url-status=dead}}</ref>

==Match==
===Team selection===
Both teams lined up in a [[Formation (association football)|4–4–2 formation]].<ref name="ESPNMatch">{{cite web|last=McGarry|first=Ian|title=United beaten at their own game|url=http://www.soccernet.com/english/news/20000814cfcmufcrep.html|publisher=[[ESPN FC|Soccernet]]|date=13 August 2000|access-date=10 March 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20000815054158/http://www.soccernet.com/english/news/20000814cfcmufcrep.html|archive-date=15 August 2000|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref name="TimesReport">{{cite news|last=McCarra|first=Kevin|url=https://link.gale.com/apps/doc/A64183291/GPS?u=wikipedia&sid=GPS&xid=77b4fd2e|title=Keane's dismissal signals red alert; Football|date=14 August 2000|work=The Times|access-date=10 March 2020|page=3|author-link=Kevin McCarra|via=Gale Academic OneFile|url-access=subscription}}</ref> [[David Beckham]] was passed fit by Ferguson to play for Manchester United after the [[midfielder]] was treated for a back injury he sustained in training.<ref name="BBCPreview" /><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://link.gale.com/apps/doc/A64085239/GPS?u=wikipedia&sid=GPS&xid=2fea5b82|title=Football: David Beckham breaks down in training|date=12 August 2000|work=The Independent|access-date=10 March 2020|page=28|via=Gale General OneFile|url-access=subscription}}</ref> [[Wes Brown]] and [[David May (footballer)|David May]] were absent with a [[cruciate ligament]] and [[Achilles tendon rupture|Achilles tendon injury]] respectively,<ref name="BBCPreview" /> and [[Jesper Blomqvist]] had not recovered from injury to return to first-team action.<ref name=TimesAbuse/> This was [[Fabien Barthez]]'s first match.<ref name="ScotsmanReport" />

Chelsea were without Spanish full-back [[Albert Ferrer]], who sustained a chest injury during the team's pre-season tour of the Netherlands that required him to rest for 10 days. [[Emerson Thome]] and [[John Terry]] also missed the game through hamstring and ankle injuries respectively.<ref>{{Cite news|last=Pryor|first=Matthew|url=https://link.gale.com/apps/doc/A64266096/GPS?u=wikipedia&sid=GPS&xid=0e2c549f|title=Vialli's line-up likely to have familiar look; Football Saturday|date=12 August 2000|work=The Times|access-date=10 March 2020|page=31|via=Gale Academic OneFile|url-access=subscription}}</ref> [[Graeme Le Saux]] began as a [[Substitute (association football)|substitute]] in his first competitive match for 10 months after being sidelined with an ankle injury that needed two minor operations.<ref name="CFCPreview" /><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://link.gale.com/apps/doc/A63314778/GPS?u=wikipedia&sid=GPS&xid=1e457522|title=Le Saux targets; Football|date=11 July 2000|work=[[Coventry Evening Telegraph]]|access-date=10 March 2020|page=42|via=Gale OneFile: News|url-access=subscription}}</ref> Vialli included his team's new signings Guðjohnsen, Hasselbaink and [[Mario Stanić]] in Chelsea's matchday squad.<ref name="CFCPreview" />

===Summary===
The match [[Kick-off (association football)|kicked off]] at 15:00 local time under cloudy skies and in front of 65,148 spectators.<ref name="CFCPreview" /><ref name="ESPNMatch" /><ref name="IndyReport">{{cite news|last=Moore|first=Glenn|url=https://link.gale.com/apps/doc/A64142430/GPS?u=wikipedia&sid=GPS&xid=9b1131f7|title=Football: Chelsea capitalise on Keane's folly; Chelsea 2 Hasselbaink 22, Melchiot 73 Manchester United 0 Half-time: 1–0 Att: 65,148|date=14 August 2000|work=The Independent|access-date=10 March 2020|page=1|via=Gale General OneFile|url-access=subscription}}</ref> Manchester United had the first chance after seven minutes, when [[Teddy Sheringham]] was [[Fouls and misconduct (association football)|fouled]] by [[Frank Leboeuf]] and the resulting [[Free kick (association football)|free-kick]] taken by Beckham went straight into the Chelsea [[Glossary of association football terms#Wall|wall]].<ref name="ManUtdReport">{{cite web|title=Keane off as United crash for charity|url=http://www.manutd.com/matches/match.sps?id=2000947928|website=ManUtd.com|publisher=Manchester United F.C|date=13 August 2000|access-date=10 March 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20001019220239/http://www.manutd.com/matches/match.sps?id=2000947928|archive-date=19 October 2000|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref name="SkySportsMatch">{{cite web|last=Hobbs|first=Tim|title=Keane off as Chelsea show no charity|url=http://www.sky.com/sports/football/matchreports/2000matchreport2052.htm|website=Sky Sports|date=13 August 2000|access-date=10 March 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20000815200044/http://www.sky.com/sports/football/matchreports/2000matchreport2052.htm|archive-date=15 August 2000|url-status=dead}}</ref> A minute later, Hasselbaink set up his teammate Stanić,<ref name="IndyReport" /> whose shot from {{Convert|12|yd||abbr=on}} went wide to the left of the Manchester United goal post.<ref name="SkySportsMatch" /><ref name="BBCClockwatch">{{cite web|title=Charity Shield clockwatch|url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport/hi/english/football/newsid_876000/876431.stm|website=BBC Sport|date=13 August 2000|access-date=10 March 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20000816165125/http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport/hi/english/football/newsid_876000/876431.stm|archive-date=16 August 2000|url-status=dead}}</ref> The first sign of tension between the players came after 15 minutes when [[Roy Keane]] and [[Gus Poyet]] clattered into each other during a [[Glossary of association football terms#Fifty-fifty|50–50 tackle]].<ref name="BBCClockwatch" /> The referee did not take any action.<ref name="ManUtdReport" /><ref name="BPReport">{{cite news|last=Bradley|first=Mark|url=https://link.gale.com/apps/doc/A64149500/GPS?u=wikipedia&sid=GPS&xid=789998f3|title=Champs hassled to distraction by improved Blues|date=14 August 2000|work=[[The Birmingham Post]]|access-date=10 March 2020|page=21|via=Gale OneFile News|url-access=subscription}}</ref> [[Gianfranco Zola]] beat [[Gary Neville]] on the left wing and put in a [[Cross (association football)|cross]],<ref name="TimesReport" /><ref name="IndyReport" /> only for Stanić to head wide from the back post.<ref name="ChelseaReport">{{cite web|title=Chelsea 2–0 Man Utd|url=http://www.chelseafc.co.uk/chelsea/news/news_13800_1820.shtml|publisher=Chelsea F.C|date=13 August 2000|access-date=10 March 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20000925174022/http://www.chelseafc.co.uk/chelsea/news/news_13800_1820.shtml|archive-date=25 September 2000|url-status=dead}}</ref> Hasselbaink then took possession when he forced [[Mikaël Silvestre]] to rush his shot which then went wide of the goal.<ref name="ScotsmanReport">{{cite news|last=Lappin|first=Tom|url=https://link.gale.com/apps/doc/A82308379/GPS?u=wikipedia&sid=GPS&xid=991dcf39|title=Charity put on hold as Keane has off day|date=14 August 2000|work=[[The Scotsman]]|access-date=10 March 2020|page=26|via=Gale OneForce News|url-access=subscription}}</ref><ref name="ManUtdReport" /><ref name="BBCClockwatch" /> Ferguson made a substitution in the 19th minute bringing on [[Jaap Stam]] for Silvestre,<ref name="ScotsmanReport" /> who had suffered a hip injury.<ref name="BBCClockwatch" />

Two minutes later, [[Ryan Giggs]] set up Ole Gunnar Solskjær who struck Manchester United's first chance to score into the [[Glossary of association football terms#Side netting|side netting]].<ref name="BBCClockwatch" /><ref name="BPReport" /> Hasselbaink opened the scoring for Chelsea in the 22nd minute by curling the ball over goalkeeper Barthez's head and past him via a deflection off Stam after being put through by a [[header (association football)|header]] from Poyet {{Convert|40|yd|m|abbr=on}} away.<ref name="TimesReport" /><ref name="ScotsmanReport" /> A tackle from [[Mario Melchiot]] stopped Sheringham, and Zola took advantage of the confused Manchester United defence between Barthez and [[Denis Irwin]] on the six-yard line.<ref name="SkySportsMatch" /><ref name="BBCClockwatch" /> The best opportunity for Manchester United came before the first half ended when Beckham's angled pass came into [[Paul Scholes]]'s path in the penalty box. Scholes received the ball with his chest and shot at goal as it came down onto his foot, but his shot went to the right of De Goey and away from goal due to pressure from Leboeuf.<ref name="ScotsmanReport" /><ref name="ManUtdReport" /><ref name="BBCClockwatch" />

[[File:Mario-Melchiot.jpg|left|thumb|[[Mario Melchiot]] scored Chelsea's second goal of the match after 72 minutes.]]
The second half began with a [[Volley (association football)|volley]] from Scholes deflecting onto the Chelsea crossbar, leading to a [[corner kick]].<ref name="BBCClockwatch" /> Barthez dived to the left to save a shot from Leboeuf and took possession of the ball.<ref name="SkySportsMatch" /><ref name="BBCClockwatch" /> In the 59th minute, a tackle on Keane by Hasselbaink prompted Keane to waggle his finger in Hasselbaink's face in anger.<ref name="ScotsmanReport" /> Beckham and referee Mike Riley suggested to Keane that he maintain his composure, which he remonstrated against.<ref name="ScotsmanReport" /><ref name="SkySportsMatch" /> Two minutes later,<ref name="IndyReport" /> Keane received a [[Fouls and misconduct (association football)|red card]] from Riley for a studs-up tackle on Poyet's calf muscle from behind.<ref name="TimesReport" /><ref name="BPReport" /><ref name="ChelseaReport" /> It was Keane's seventh red card in seven seasons at Manchester United, and resulted in a three-match ban.<ref name="IndyReport" /> Ferguson did not immediately re-organise his side and left three players in the midfield.<ref name="ManUtdReport" /> He made Manchester United's second change in the 70th minute, when he brought on [[Dwight Yorke]] and [[Andy Cole]] for Sheringham and Solskjær to try and draw 1–1.<ref name="ManUtdReport" /><ref name="BBCClockwatch" /> Meanwhile, Chelsea brought on [[Jody Morris]] for [[Roberto Di Matteo]].<ref name="SkySportsMatch" />

In the 72nd minute, Chelsea extended their lead to 2–0 when Melchiot [[Dribbling#Association football|dribbled]] down the right to the edge of the [[Penalty area|penalty box]] and knocked the ball low with his left foot between Stam's legs and past Barthez into the far post from {{Convert|18|yd|m|abbr=on}}.<ref name="ScotsmanReport" /><ref name="SkySportsMatch" /><ref name="BPReport" /> Le Saux came on for Poyet in the 77th minute and immediately set up Hasselbaink, whose header went wide of the post.<ref name="BBCClockwatch" /> [[Quinton Fortune]] replaced Giggs a minute later. Scholes received a yellow card for a tackle on Morris after 81 minutes, and then had a shot which went over the Chelsea goal. The remaining six minutes of the match passed without further incident, and Chelsea won 2–0.<ref name="SkySportsMatch" /> It was the second time Chelsea had won the Charity Shield,<ref name="ChelseaReport" /> while Manchester United had lost in the Charity Shield for the third year in a row after defeats to Arsenal in 1998 and 1999.<ref name="ManUtdReport" /><ref name="DTReport">{{Cite news|last=Collett|first=Mike|date=14 August 2000|title=Chelsea show no charity|page=62|work=The Daily Telegraph|url=https://link.gale.com/apps/doc/A103648910/GPS?u=wikipedia&sid=GPS&xid=302e0c65|url-access=subscription|access-date=11 March 2020|via=Gale OneFile: News}}</ref>

==Post-match==
During the presentation of medals in the Royal Box, Chelsea chairman [[Ken Bates]] attempted to hang a blue and white joke medal inscribed with the words ''Lord Fergie, the best thing since sliced bread'' around the neck of Ferguson as a peace offering, after the latter had likened the former to [[Mao Zedong]] in his autobiography. Ferguson refused the medal and Bates said: "I wanted to try to calm things down but he wouldn't take it and that says more about him than me."<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/teams/c/chelsea/879692.stm|title=Bates' gift to 'Lord Fergie'|date=14 August 2000|website=BBC Sport|access-date=11 March 2020}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|last=Millar|first=Ken|url=https://link.gale.com/apps/doc/A64184692/GPS?u=wikipedia&sid=GPS&xid=940dc74e|title=Fergie turns down 'medal' Football|date=14 August 2000|work=Coventry Evening Telegraph|access-date=11 March 2020|page=43|via=Gale OneFile: News|url-access=subscription}}</ref>

Vialli said he was delighted with the result and praised the form of his players: "It was a real match. The players performed in a very convincing way."<ref>{{Cite news|last=Williams|first=Richard|url=https://link.gale.com/apps/doc/A75726280/GPS?u=wikipedia&sid=GPS&xid=e188eb56|title=Football: Charity Shield: Keane's crime of passion: Chelsea 2 Manchester United 0|date=14 August 2000|work=The Guardian|access-date=11 March 2020|page=1|author-link=Richard Williams (journalist)|via=Gale General OneFile|url-access=subscription}}</ref> He praised his players and stated he did not wish to be overexcited: "I'm sure the Manchester United players will feel this defeat and will be spot on for the first league game. We have to be the same against [[West Ham United F.C.|West Ham]] otherwise this victory won't count for anything. If we get carried away I am sure West Ham will make it very difficult for us."<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.sky.com/sports/football/premier/chelsea/story3.htm|title=Vialli Knows Danger of Beating Man Utd|date=13 August 2000|website=Sky Sports|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20000815200100/http://www.sky.com/sports/football/premier/chelsea/story3.htm|archive-date=15 August 2000|access-date=11 March 2020}}</ref> Ferguson commented on his team: "It was a game we were looking to help produce the sharpness we usually have. We played pretty football but without a cutting edge."<ref name="IndyReport" /> Sheringham believed that Chelsea were deserved winners, saying: "In that sense it was a good run-out and as long as we're right for then, we will be very happy. That's what it's all geared to."<ref name=TNLPostMatch>{{Cite news|last=Barlow|first=Matt|url=https://link.gale.com/apps/doc/A64192059/GPS?u=wikipedia&sid=GPS&xid=c4b8da4a|title=Football: Jimmy's so sorry|date=15 August 2000|work=[[The News Letter]]|access-date=11 March 2020|page=31|via=Gale OneFile: News|url-access=subscription}}</ref>

Ferguson argued that Riley had created the incident that saw Keane sent off for his tackle on Poyet: "The referee waited too long to act. There were a lot of players going in hard right throughout the game. You have to be fair to both camps and we were just waiting to see how long he (Riley) was going to leave it. It is a showpiece occasion but if someone commits a yellow card offence, the appropriate action should be taken."<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://theworldgame.sbs.com.au/fergie-fuming-again|title=Fergie fuming again|date=14 August 2000|work=[[The World Game]]|access-date=11 March 2020}}</ref> Hasselbaink apologised to Keane and said he had made an error in the earlier tackle.<ref name=TNLPostMatch/><ref name=IndyPostMatch>{{Cite news|last=Tynan|first=Gordon|url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football/premier-league/chelsea-striker-issues-apology-to-keane-696372.html |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/archive/20220501/https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football/premier-league/chelsea-striker-issues-apology-to-keane-696372.html |archive-date=1 May 2022 |url-access=subscription|title=Chelsea striker issues apology to Keane|date=15 August 2000|work=The Independent|access-date=11 March 2020}}{{cbignore}}</ref> The Referees' Association president [[Peter Willis (referee)|Peter Willis]] expressed concern that the Premier League will become "a bloodbath" if there was continued scrutiny of "officials' performances":  "All of us accept that football is an emotional game, we can make errors of judgement in challenges but there was no misinterpretation of what happened yesterday and I don't think Sir Alex Ferguson can argue against that."<ref name=IndyPostMatch/>

Manchester United retained the Premier League during the [[2000–01 FA Premier League|2000–01 season]], which they won by ten points from second-placed Arsenal. Chelsea struggled in the league, losing eleven games as they finished in sixth, nineteen points behind United.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.rsssf.org/tablese/eng01.html |title=England 2000/01 |date=15 February 2006 |access-date=8 June 2021 |first1=Ian |first2=Stephen |last1=King |website=[[RSSSF]] |last2=Mulrine }}</ref>
